2	title: Remove Silences
3	description: Find the dead air in a spoken recording, see it on the timeline, and cut it all as one edit.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Remove Silences finds the dead air in a spoken recording, shows you what it would cut, and takes it all out as one undo step, closing the timeline over each cut.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Remove Silences…"
14	  tools={['detect_silence', 'ripple_delete_ranges']}
15	  needs="Nothing. Voice detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## Remove the silences
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Choose **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…**. It's available when the timeline has a clip with its sound on. If there turns out to be nothing to measure, Frame Job beeps instead of opening the sheet.
23	
24	2. Check what's shaded on the timeline, and read the count in the sheet, for example "23 cuts · removes 00:00:04:12". Both update as you change a control. With nothing to cut the count reads "No cuts" and **Remove** is dimmed.
25	
26	3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls) until the cuts look right.
27	
28	4. Choose **Remove**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	<Shot
33	  name="14-remove-silences-sheet.sheet"
34	  alt="The Remove Silences sheet, with Judge by set to Voice, a Level if no voice slider at −40 dBFS, Longer than 0.5 seconds, Keep at ends 0.1 seconds, and In set to All audible clips."
35	/>
36	
37	The sheet opens on its defaults every time. It doesn't remember your last settings.
38	
39	## The controls
40	
41	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
42	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
43	| **Judge by:** | How a moment is tested. See [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/). | Voice, or Level if the voice model can't be used | Voice, Level |
44	| **Quieter than:** or **Level if no voice:** | The level that counts as quiet. The row reads **Quieter than:** in Level mode and **Level if no voice:** in Voice mode. | −40 dBFS | −80 to −10 dBFS |
45	| **Longer than:** | The shortest quiet stretch worth cutting. Shorter pauses, such as the gap between two words, stay. | 0.5 s | 0.05 to 10 s |
46	| **Keep at ends:** | How much of each quiet stretch to keep at each end, so speech doesn't start or stop abruptly. | 0.1 s | 0 to 2 s |
47	| **In:** | Whether to look at **Selected clips** or **All audible clips**. | Selected clips when the selection has something audible, otherwise All audible clips | |
48	
49	The level row is a slider in whole decibels, with its value beside it. In Level mode, sound at or below it is quiet. In Voice mode, it judges clips that hold no voice, and a clip the mix turns down to it or lower is quiet whatever it contains.
50	
51	**Selected clips** is greyed out when nothing selected makes a sound, and a selection of muted clips counts as nothing audible, as does a selected nest. Choose it to stop a music bed under a voice-over from holding the cuts up.
52	
53	**Longer than:** measures the stretch as you hear it, before **Keep at ends:** takes its share. A stretch no longer than twice **Keep at ends:** isn't cut. Cuts then snap to the frame grid, so up to a frame more of room tone can remain at each end. Raise **Keep at ends:** if a word gets clipped.
54	
55	The two number fields take up to two decimal places. A number outside the range stays in the field and **Remove** beeps until you fix it.
56	
57	The count and the shading follow the slider as it moves, and a number field when you leave it.
58	
59	## What the sheet tells you
60	
61	The sheet explains itself under the count. It can show more than one of these at once.
62	
63	| The sheet says | What it means |
64	| --- | --- |
65	| "Nothing in this timeline is audible, so nothing was analysed." | Nothing in scope makes a sound. With **Selected clips** it reads "Nothing the selected clips play is audible in the mix, so nothing was analysed." |
66	| "The waveform is still being analysed for …" or "Speech is still being analysed for …" | Frame Job hasn't finished with the files it names, which often happens straight after an import. Leave the sheet open and it updates as each one lands. |
67	| "Nothing inside is proposed for removal yet." | Follows the line above: nothing in those files can be cut until their analysis lands. |
68	| "Anything inside it that holds no voice is left alone until it lands…" | Follows the waveform line in Voice mode: speech can already be judged, but a clip with no voice has to wait for the waveform. It may add that the mix already turns a clip down far enough to be quiet. |
69	| "What is proposed inside … is quiet in the MIX…" | The named clips are still waiting for analysis, but they've been turned down, faded or ducked far enough to be quiet, so those cuts stand whatever the analysis finds. |
70	| "Quiet inside a nest is left alone…" | A quiet stretch at least as long as **Longer than:** ran across a nest. There may be dead air inside it, so a low count doesn't mean there's none. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and remove its silences there. With several nests it reads "Quiet inside 2 nests…". |
71	
72	Relinking a file starts its analysis again. If an agent relinks one while the sheet is open, the sheet drops the old answers at once and updates when the new ones land.
73	
74	## Good to know
75	
76	- A gap with nothing audible in it is left alone, and so is a stretch where only a muted clip plays. Remove Silences takes dead air out of a recording, not the gaps you placed between clips. [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) does that.
77	- With **Selected clips**, a moment none of those clips covers is never cut.
78	- Nothing inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) is cut, because a nest plays from its first frame and a cut into one would strand the rest of it.
79	- A quiet stretch broken up by a nest or a transition is measured in its pieces.
80	
81	## With an agent
82	
83	`detect_silence` reads the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. Pass them to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
84	
85	An agent isn't held to the sheet's ranges, and it can also set how sure the voice model must be, which the sheet doesn't offer. To look inside a nest, it opens the nest with `set_scope` and reads again.
86	
87	## Related
88	
89	- [What counts as silent](/cleanup/voice-or-level/)
90	- [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/)
91	- [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/)

title: "Tools: clean-up"
description: "The agent tools that find silences and filler words as ranges, make a filler transcript, and cut what they found."
---

These tools find what [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) would cut. The two `detect_` tools change nothing, so you can read and adjust their ranges before making the cut.

Neither `detect_` tool takes `scope`. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

## Cut what the tools found

Pass the `ranges` from `detect_silence` or `detect_fillers` to [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). That's what **Remove** does in each sheet, and it makes the whole cut one undo step.

```json
{ "ranges": [[1200000, 1500000], [3000000, 3240000]] }
```

An agent isn't held to the ranges it was given: it can drop some or change them first. `ripple_delete_ranges` takes `scope` like any edit, so it can reach a nest without opening it. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## `detect_silence`

Finds the quiet stretches of the timeline and reports them, changing nothing. It's the read half of **Clip ▸ Remove Silences…**, see [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).

The voice model runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | No | Analyse only these clips, like the sheet's **Selected clips**. At least one. Default: the current selection when it holds anything with sound, otherwise every audible clip. |
| `mode` | string | No | `voice` judges by the voice model, falling back to level over a clip that holds no voice. `level` judges by level alone. Default: `voice`. |
| `voice_confidence` | number | No | Voice mode only. The model's probability, 0.1 to 0.9, at or above which a moment counts as speech. Default: 0.5. The sheet doesn't offer this. |
| `threshold_db` | number | No | Quieter than this counts as silence, in dBFS in the mix, at or below 0. Default: −40. |
| `min_length` | integer | No | The shortest quiet run worth cutting, in ticks. Default: 300,000 (0.5 s). |
| `padding` | integer | No | How much to leave at each end of a run, in ticks. Default: 60,000 (0.1 s). |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

`min_length` and `padding` run exactly as sent. Only the finished ranges go on the frame grid, and they snap inward, which can leave a frame of room tone rather than clip the next word. Each takes 0 to 9,000,000,000,000,000.

Quiet is measured in the mix, so a clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and another track's solo all count. In either mode, a moment the mix alone turns down to `threshold_db` or below is quiet.

A moment no clip in scope covers isn't a candidate, because a hole in the timeline isn't dead air. A nest clip is a wall: no range reaches into one.

**Answers:**

| Key | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| `ranges`, `count`, `removes` | The spans as `[from, to]` pairs in ticks, how many, and how many ticks they remove. |
| `scope`, `clips` | `selected` or `audible`, and the clips that ran. This `scope` is about clips, not nests. |
| `mode`, `threshold_db`, `min_length`, `padding`, `voice_confidence` | What actually ran. |
| `judged_by_level`, `judged_by_level_clips` | The media and the clips judged by level because they hold no voice. |
| `proposed_by_mix_clips` | Each clip a range is proposed inside only because the mix turns it down while its analysis is still running. |
| `pending_peaks` | Media still being analysed, for either the waveform or speech. Call again shortly. |
| `voice_pending` | Media whose speech is still being analysed. |
| `protected_nests` | Each nest clip a quiet run of at least `min_length` crossed. There may be dead air inside. |
| `note` | Sentences on any of the above. |
| `project` | The [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |

`proposed_by_mix_clips`, `pending_peaks`, `voice_pending`, `protected_nests` and `note` appear only when they have something to report. To look inside a protected nest, open it with `set_scope` and call again.

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

28-## What these tools share
29-
30-- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid before anything happens. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

    private func style(_ field: NSTextField, range: ClosedRange<Double>) {
        let formatter = NumberFormatter()
        formatter.numberStyle = .decimal
        formatter.allowsFloats = true
        formatter.minimumFractionDigits = 0
        formatter.maximumFractionDigits = 2
        formatter.minimum = NSNumber(value: range.lowerBound)

        field.formatter = formatter

        DSField.style(field)
    }

- **The service can miss a filler.** A filler AssemblyAI doesn't return isn't cut. A filler it returns that isn't on the list stays in, both in the cut and in captions.
- **Protection needs a transcript.** A filler cut is kept away from speech in another clip only when that clip's file has a transcript. Speech on another unlocked track with no transcript isn't protected.
- **Up to a frame can remain.** Inward frame snapping can leave a frame of room tone, or of a filler, behind.
- **Wait for analysis.** After import, Remove Silences proposes nothing inside a file until its analysis is ready: the waveform in Level mode, the voice analysis in Voice mode (and the waveform too for a clip with no voice), except where the mix already makes it quiet.
- **Voice mode can miss a soft first word** in a quiet recording; raise **Keep at ends:** if a word is clipped.
- **Singing and voice-like instruments** may read as speech.
- **A clip that holds any voice is judged by voice for its whole length**, so a long music clip with a little speech in it isn't judged by level. Limit the scope (**In:** Selected clips) to keep music out.
- **A voice panned hard to one side** sounds quieter to the voice model.
- **In a reversed clip** a cut edge can be off by up to 32 ms.
- **Nests and transitions block cuts.** Quiet or fillers inside a nest, or in a transition's overlap, are never cut from outside the nest. Open the nest first.

See also: [Editing](editing.md) for ripple delete and Close Gap, [Audio](audio.md) for volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, which all affect what Remove Silences hears, and [MCP](mcp.md) for the full tool reference.
